author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Communities across Rhode Island will gather Friday to mark 25 years since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, with ceremonies scheduled from Exeter to Newport.

The day begins at 8:30 a.m. at the Rhode Island Veterans Cemetery Wall of Honor in Exeter. Warwick, East Providence and Central Falls have events set for 10 a.m., while West Greenwich plans a 10:28 a.m. observance on the Town Hall lawn. New England Institute of Technology will hold its annual ceremony at 11 a.m. in East Greenwich.

In Newport, a remembrance ceremony and wreath-laying are scheduled for noon at the U.S. Naval War College. The Rhode Island Fire Academy in Exeter will hold a separate service at 3:30 p.m. Public-safety departments, municipal officials and community groups are organizing many of the observances.

The statewide schedule reflects the anniversary’s continuing local resonance for families, first responders and military communities. Organizers advise attendees to verify event details before traveling because schedules may change. Similar services are planned across southeastern Massachusetts, including ceremonies in Attleboro, Fall River, Easton and Somerset.
dek: Observances across the state mark the attacks’ 25th anniversary with memorial services, wreath-laying and tributes led by public-safety agencies.
headline: Rhode Island communities hold September 11 remembrance ceremonies
